## Verdicts

Verdicts 14 and 15 are open, the play's seed step on run 44078576705 and the play not opening on run
44089619689. Verdicts 1 to 13 are settled, said under each in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md.

14. **The play's seed step read the world before the new one came.** Build run 44078576705 of
    `ac5602d`, item 214, ended red at 13:58 on 2026-11-17 in its play job alone, the three test jobs
    green. Every step up to the menu's button and the death screen passed, at 3,330 s. The seed's
    field step then failed within seconds, where the green run before it spent 246 s there, with the
    world read as the overworld of seed 1 where 12345 was typed and pasted. The game's log ends with
    one frame making a pipeline of bits.slang in 3,328 ms on the runner's CPU device. The step
    presses Enter, waits three frames and reads voxel.state, and since item 214 the first frames of
    a new world are drawn behind the loading screen, so on a slow device three frames after Enter
    the state may still tell the world before. Local plays on the GPU pass. Asked, a read of which
    it is, the step reading too soon or the typed seed lost; where it reads too soon, the step waits
    for the state to tell a world opened after Enter, bounded in time, and every other step that
    reads the state within a few frames of a world's opening is read for the same; where the seed is
    lost, the mend in the game with a test. The four commits held behind it go up with the mend in
    one push.

15. **The play did not open on the engine's 6.2.102.** Build run 44089619689 of `2f23c46` ended red
    at 14:17 on 2026-11-17 in its play job alone, the three test jobs green. The game exited with
    code 1 at the open, 4.3 s in. Its session log says slangc was not found, so shaders load from
    their caches only, 64 stages read from the caches and none compiled, and then that terrain.slang
    is not in the shader cache. The job's step before had found slangc 2026.18.2 at
    build/tools/slang of the game's checkout, restored from the cache. The first local play of the
    pin stopped the same way and passed once ENGINE_SLANGC named a slangc, and the workflow sets no
    such name. Asked, a read of why the engine at 6.2.102 does not find the slangc the game's
    checkout holds, where the play before the pin compiled or read terrain.slang, the walk from the
    program's folder, the folder's shape or the name looked for among the candidates; the mend where
    it belongs, in the game's workflow and play script where the game must name it, and told to the
    review as the engine's where the engine's walk changed; and the pack workflow read for the same,
    with the word of item 216's Reply that a packed game never meets a missing cache proved by a
    pack run's game opening with no slangc. Verdict 14's mend is not yet read on a CPU device, the
    play not having reached its steps.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 The old game is replaced in place, its history kept; 2 The license stays MIT; 3 `e3d`
comes from the engine's checkout; 4 What the game finds the engine lacks goes to the engine's
ASKS.md, as before; 5 Prose is technical and generic; 6 Development resumes; the sky, the shadows
and the icons are the game's week; 7 Nothing in the sky faces the camera; the sun, the moon and the
stars are fixed on the sky and turn with the hour; 8 The mobs' sizes and models may be the other
game's, since they are numbers; 9 The tonemapping is the engine's somewhat boring curve; 10 The
review's files are committed by the batch that comes next, and by the reviewer at most once a day;
11 The list of 2026-10-20 at 23:30, in the reviewer's order; 12 Compute shaders for generation, the
direction of 2026-10-21; 13 The chosen packs set the look, read from the player's copy and never
shipped; 14 A modpack is the reference of the game's feel, read for shapes, numbers and ideas, and
nothing of it ships; 15 The six candidates of Decision 14 are taken; 16 The screen probes stay off
in the game, and the cascades' faults go to the engine; 17 The windows after Recolourful Containers
and the HUD after Bare Bones, read from the player's packs, and the game's own art moved toward
them; 18 The three packs are not shipped and are fetched at first start instead; 19 A screenshot on
F2; 20 Simple Grass Flowers as a fourth default pack, through block state variants; 21 The look the
game aims at is the modpack's gallery; 22 Packs give pictures alone, and every rule is the game's
own; 23 The look without a pack takes Bare Bones' colors; 24 The README's pictures, an animation at
its head and pictures in its parts; 25 Three words during item 46's scouting, the sky's bodies cut,
the rifts in villages and the sun's look; 26 The engine's F1 and F3 come to the game; 27 More
vegetation, and the plants cast shadows; 28 The blades like the modpack's, and the light and the
grade from the shader settings it is played with; 29 The sun's shadows step on a grid of eight a
block; 30 The mobs take Bare Bones' entity pictures; 31 The zombie's own face is the source's
archetype, the villager's eyes lower; 32 The Bare Bones x Fresh Animations pack is the fourth
default pack, above Bare Bones; 33 The creeper keeps the vanilla look, the game's own art, under
every pack; 34 The observations of 2026-10-23 and their order; 35 Trees fell as one and gravity
blocks fall; 36 Glass and water reflect nothing for the present; 37 Branches are named for their
work, never claude/ or a random string, and work stays on main where one session writes; 38 The
empty hand shows no arm; 39 A devlog under `.github/devlog`, and AGENTS.md's rows for it and for the
pushes; 40 Far land at 32 columns by default, the render distance kept at 12; 41 Far land goes; 42
The screen probes are off by default; 43 The game uses the engine's ECS where it fits, beside the
loop; 44 The clouds cover the area about the player and do not reach the horizon; 45 A session saves
the pictures of its work in the repository, N 4.8; 46 The README's pictures taken again, an
animation at its head and pictures in its parts (Decision 24); 47 The devlog written as the work
goes; 48 The screen probes are on, off a debugging switch alone; 49 The devlog carries notes beside
the pictures; 50 The F3 window's parts find their homes; 51 The far cascade is on by default and the
shadow distance is 128 blocks; 52 A voxel engine in Rust is the reference for the game's
performance; 53 No far land in the game; 54 Held lights are plain lights without shadows; 55 A
reading's picture explains itself, and a plain capture or pair stays where it shows the thing; 56
Every picture a session makes goes to the repository's dump folder; 57 The version's major and minor
move by the reviewer's judgment; 58 No one is named in a picture, each in full under Decisions in
REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md.

59. **Anisotropic filtering at 16 everywhere.** Decided on 2026-11-04 at 11:07, anisotropic
   filtering is at 16 everywhere, since it is cheap and looks better at steep angles. So every
   sampler that reads a texture, color, normal, surface or atlas, filters anisotropically at 16, or
   at the device's most where it offers less, at every quality and with no knob; the shadow, probe
   and table samplers that are not textures keep their own filters. The game's textures read through
   the engine's samplers, so it comes with the engine's item 201 and the next package; the game sets
   nothing. Added at 11:40, the game is pixel filtering and needs no change, so its atlas stays at
   Point and item 156 is closed.

60. **Version tags.** Decided at about 14:00 on 2026-11-08, after every commit of the Unity
    Essentials repositories was tagged as `v2.0.30` and the like, the three projects take tags too,
    with the review's questions answered at 14:1x. The form is `v6.0.91`, the letter v before
    `build/version.sh`'s number. Tags go on each major or minor change and on the commits packages
    were built from, since a tag on every commit clutters the list and is unnecessary, the tags
    marking releases some time apart with meaningful changes and not commits apart. The major and
    the minor are the sessions' to raise, each session working on the project deciding when the time
    is right to raise the minor or the major, every commit counting as a patch, with full liberty
    once a step is done and meaningful changes were made. N 6.3 holds the rule and the reviewer sets
    the tags as it pushes. `v0.2.0` marks `7e052e8`, which set 0.2 (Decision 57), set at 14:12; a
    release build of `build/publish.sh` is tagged when the owner names one. Decision 57 stands with
    the game's session able to raise the version as well as the reviewer.

61. **No personal name in any repository.** On 2026-11-08 at about 15:25 the account's code search
    was shown finding the personal name in six files of four repositories, this game's `LICENSE`
    among them, after the ask of the same morning that the name stand nowhere, and at about 15:27
    the ask followed that the game's license be the Mozilla Public License Version 2.0, as the
    engines' are; the MPL names no holder. The history's authors are not rewritten here, since the
    review's files, the devlog and the package's release notes cite the commits by their hashes, and
    the commits' noreply address is the account's already.

62. **No middle dot.** Decided at 17:57 and 18:00 on 2026-11-08, the middle dot is not used, the
    README's top links separated by a space alone and the dot nowhere else; the reviewer changed the
    README's first line in the tree on that decision, for the next commit to carry (item 159). The
    rule goes into STYLE.md's Punctuation as the shared text has it everywhere.

63. **Comments on the code's own terms.** A comment of scenes_sponza was read at about 19:00 on
    2026-11-08, "The frame graded as that scene's HDRP profile grades it, by the look of its AgX -
    Powerful.exr, a lookup build/unity-lut.py writes from that strip, a gamma of w 0.225, and a
    bloom of intensity 0.25, threshold 0.333 and scatter 0.7, worked out as HDRP works them out",
    and found to read badly, to read as an em dash does, and to lean too far on outside knowledge
    and on the sessions' knowledge of work in progress, in scenes_sponza explicitly and probably
    everywhere else. The rule from it, in STYLE.md's Register and as N 4.11, is that a comment
    stands on the code's own terms. It says what the code does and why in the engine's words; a
    number taken from elsewhere stands with the reason it is right here, what it makes the frame or
    the program do, and the source is named once in the documents' references and not in the
    comment; the file names of outside assets, another product's profile or process as the
    explanation, "as X works it out", and the facts of the sessions' work are not written in a
    comment. Item 159 carries STYLE.md's sentence and the game's own sweep.

64. **A fault seen in motion is read in motion.** Reported at 17:25 on 2026-11-09, the game's global
    illumination has looked noisy the same way for weeks, and the review's answer read only the
    shader cache. The readings here since 2026-10-24 were settled stills, which a fault in motion
    passes, so a fault named while moving is read from a recording, one handed in where there is one
    and a scripted walk and turn offscreen where not, picture to picture, with the standing, the
    walking, the turning and the two seconds after a stop each given their share of pixels moved,
    and the review asks for a recording and the settings file when a fault is named without one. The
    engine's Decision 107 says the same; put up for approval as its Decision 95's precedent allows.
    Item 166. Approved on 2026-11-11, asked by the review with N 7.9, N 7.10 and N 7.11.

## Replies

What else of the game the engine's origin of 264 changes the meaning of, read at `f201940` against
the engine's 6.2.60-local.264.6 (`3768c988`), with no change made. The engine keeps a world-number
twin of each lighting function that takes a point (`lights.slang:750-769`), which takes the origin
off again (`placeOf`), and the `world` of a pixel is its place plus the origin, so every use below
reads as before. With the game's origin on, the world numbers stay under about 5,000 blocks, where a
float's step is a 2,048th of a block, and none of them shows.

- `bits.slang:17` reads the instance's translation, a place since 264, and the settled edit adds
  `modelPush.origin` to it. A second form keeps the place there and sets `middle.place` in place of
  `middle.world` at `bits.slang:44-45`, with no round trip.
- `terrain.slang:275` and `:287` snap the sun's shadow's point to eighths in world numbers
  (`pixelMiddle(input.world, ...)`) and hand it to `lightReaching`, which takes the origin off
  again. `lightReachingPlaced(pixelMiddle(input.place, ...))` snaps to the same eighths, the
  engine's origin being whole blocks, and is the trial that mended the stripes with the game's
  origin off.
- `terrain.slang:176`, `:298`, `:350` and `:356` take the block, the rim and the texture's place
  from world numbers by `floor` and `frac`. The place gives the same values, the origin being whole
  blocks, where `block` and the texture's place change together.
- `terrain.slang:410` calls `mirrored(..., world, ...)`, and `mirroredPlaced(..., place, ...)` takes
  no round trip.
- `terrain.slang:420` reads the haze by the world's height, `world.y`, which stays a world number.
- `mob.slang:27-28` call `arriving` and `lightReaching` with `input.world`, and their `Placed` twins
  take `input.place`. `mob.slang:65` sets `up.world` from `input.base.world`, which setting
  `up.place` from `input.base.place` does without the round trip.
- No game shader reads a matrix of the engine's. `terrain.slang:168` reads the instance's color and
  not its rows, and `cavefields.slang` works in the land's whole columns outside the engine's
  drawing.
- On the CPU, `WaterMirror.cs:43` and `GameCommands.cs:745` and `:773` cast the engine's rays from
  the screen and `Measurements.cs:197`, `:243` and `:263` take its points to the screen, whose
  working 264 changed and the rehearsal read alike with the game's origin on. `HeldLights.cs:66-71`
  and `BlastEffects.cs:104` and `:122` hand the engine world points it places itself.

Nothing beyond the bits' edit changes meaning as the game ships. The `Placed` twins are the forms
that stay exact where a place's numbers are small and a world's are not.

The game's side of the engine's part 7, read on 6.2.60 with the game at `f201940` as it ships, from
copies of the review's copy of the data, at 1280 by 720 with the frame unlimited, under the
exclusive lock on tuned's powersave-bazzite, three runs.

What `Recenter` does in its frame (`VoxelGame.cs:546-564`), called from `Begin` (`:645`) before
anything is stepped or drawn. The step is to the multiple of 1,024 nearest the player once it is
4,096 out along x or z (`LandOrigin.cs:84-98`), so a walk or a flight moves the origin 4,096 at once
and a teleport by any multiple of 1,024, and y never moves. In order:

1. `Renderer.Shift` (`ChunkRenderer.cs:952-984`) uploads every section part's mesh again, uploads
   the lamps' cubes again (`MakeLampCubes`, `:679`), gives every part and group a new `Transform`,
   moves the emitters' matrices, marks every group's faces changed and has the lamps gathered again.
2. Every ECS `Body`, the player's and the camera with it, every arrow and every blast moves by the
   step.
3. The mobs' homes and last places (`Mob.cs:193`), the fall's last height (`Vitals.cs:74`), the
   steps' voices (`GameSounds.cs:88`), the blasts' clouds and flashes, set again in the engine by
   `SetParticleEmitterPosition` and `SetLightPosition` (`BlastEffects.cs:112-124`), the bits' bodies
   (`BlockBits.cs:88`) and the rings on the water (`AmbientParticles.cs:137`) move by it.
4. `LandOrigin.MoveTo` last. The held torch's light is set from the hand the next frame, and the sky
   takes no place.

So the engine is handed again every section's mesh as a new one, every part's matrix moved by the
step, the lamps' cubes as new meshes and the camera moved by the step, all in one frame.

What the engine does with it on 6.2.60:

- **The step's frame** costs 228 to 242 ms at Low and 250 ms at High (the game's clamp, 409 ms of
  work in the frame), where the slowest frame of a flight crossing no step is 38.5 to 52.7 ms and
  42.5 to 50.9 ms. Of it, the game's re-upload in its update takes 117 to 133 ms, the engine's
  `prepare.GpuMeshesPrepare` 81 to 89 ms, a collection 25.5 to 28.7 ms, the field 10.2 to 10.8 ms
  and, at High, `cpu.global_illumination` 164 ms, the ray scene built again for every mesh.
- **A flight of 600 frames** east across a step against one across none reads a median of 8.97 to
  9.19 ms against 8.07 to 8.09 at Low and 12.03 to 12.10 against 9.03 to 9.06 at High, and a 99th
  part of 33.8 to 52.7 against 32.4 to 33.4 at Low and 61.7 to 62.8 against 33.8 to 37.6 at High.
- **The field** after a hop of three blocks in one frame across a step holds the change after 14 to
  26 frames, 0.2 to 1.6 million triangles splatted as every mesh is built in again, where a hop
  across none changes it not at all. After a flight across a step it holds after 235 to 267 frames
  at Low and 45 to 46 at High, the flight's own builds among them, against 8 to 188 and 14 to 15
  across none.
- **The light** changes once, 8 to 11 frames after the step, as the field's build ends. Recorded
  frame by frame with the clouds off, 0.75% of the pixels pass 8 levels at High in that frame and
  0.5% at Low, along the land's edges, the most 58 to 60 levels, and the land's mean falls 0.28
  levels, where a hop across none shows no change. No light drops visibly, so no picture pair is
  made. The glow lights, 89 to 98 carried and the 64 nearest lit, show no change of their own. The
  frames are `03-01-part7-step-light-high.png` and `-low.png` in the dump.

What the game would call, and when. In `Recenter`, after `StepTo` (`VoxelGame.cs:549`) and before
anything moves, in the update of the frame whose draws the engine then extracts, the call with the
step as it is, `(-4096, 0, 0)` for a flight east across x 8,192, a multiple of 1,024 along x and z
and 0 along y. Every such step is a whole count of every cell of the game's field as the game sets
it (`LightSettings.cs:22-33`), cells of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 and a far cascade's of 4, of their snap
of eight cells, 2 to 32 blocks, of the probes' spacing and of the engine's origin's 16-block step,
1,024 being 32 times 32. The game keeps moving its own places and its entities' `Transform`s by the
step as it does, and stops uploading every section's mesh and the lamps' cubes again and marking
every group's faces changed (`ChunkRenderer.cs:954-962`, `:978`). The call meets its contract where
the engine takes every mesh drawn the next frame at its matrix plus the step as the same still mesh,
moves its field's cascades, its probes, its frame before's view, its shadows' fits and its render
origin by the step and keeps their contents, so the step's frame costs what a frame crossing none
does and the field and the light change by nothing.

Verdict 15's read. The engine's walk for slangc changed between 6.2.86 and 6.2.102, in its commit
`b634f33d`, "the shader compiler is taken from the nearest checkout of the engine alone and only
where the user owns it". At 6.2.86 `SlangCompiler.Locate` walked up from the program's folder and
from the working directory and took `build/tools/slang/bin/slangc` in any folder it passed, so the
play's game in `VoxelSandbox/bin/Debug/net10.0` found the one `build/fetch-slang.sh` puts in the
game's checkout, and compiled the terrain shader there on a runner whose cache was empty. The green
run of `fc4a632` on 6.2.86 logs no "slangc was not found" where the red one logs it. At 6.2.102 the
walk (`SlangCompiler.FromCheckout`) stops at the nearest folder that holds `3DEngine.slnx` and takes
its `build/tools` alone, so a game's checkout, which holds `VoxelSandbox.slnx`, gives none, and a
game on the package finds slangc only by `ENGINE_SLANGC`. That is the engine's change, made on
purpose so no program runs a compiler from a folder others may write, and the game names its own:

- The build workflow's play job and the pack workflow's shaders job name `ENGINE_SLANGC` as the
  checkout's slangc once `build/fetch-slang.sh` has fetched it.
- `build/play.sh` and `build/shaders.sh` name the checkout's slangc where none is named, so a local
  run needs no setting.
- `build/fetch-slang.sh` and `build/fetch-slang.ps1` end by saying the line that names it, and their
  notes and the README's Running it say the engine looks in a checkout of the engine alone.

The pack workflow's `build/shaders.sh` runs `./e3d shaders` out of `.engine`, whose `build/tools`
holds no slangc, so it would have failed the same way on 6.2.102. A packed game carries the shaders
it compiled and needs no compiler, which a pack run after the build proves.
